title: 24-hour blood pressure monitoring for teens
what: Your teen wears a cuff on the upper arm for 24 hours. A small device on the belt measures blood pressure by itself, day and night.
why: For high blood pressure at a visit, headaches, nosebleeds, before sports, or to check treatment.
duration: usually worn for 24 hours; the report is usually ready in 1 to 2 days
tell_doctor: Their daily routine: school, sports, training
What bothers them: headaches, nosebleeds, dizziness
If blood pressure was measured before, and what the numbers were

prepare.title: Routine
prepare.text: A normal day: school and walks. Better to skip hard training that day. Ask the doctor.

prepare.title: Clothing
prepare.text: A T-shirt with a wide, loose sleeve, and a loose top over it.

prepare.title: Shower
prepare.text: No washing with the device on. Shower before it is put on.

bring: The diary the clinic gives you, and a pen
steps: The cuff goes on the upper arm, usually the non-dominant arm
The device is clipped to the belt
They explain how to keep the diary
During the day, the device usually measures every 15 to 30 minutes, less often at night
During a measurement, keep the arm still and down
After 24 hours, the device is removed at the clinic
feel: The cuff squeezes the arm at each measurement
Night measurements may wake your teen. That is normal
after: After removal, back to normal life
The report is usually ready in 1 to 2 days
Go over the results with your pediatrician or a cardiologist

faq.q: Can my teen go to school with the device?
faq.a: Yes. Normal activity helps show how blood pressure changes.
When they slept, ate, exercised, took medicines, and anything that bothered them.

reminders.text: The 24-hour blood pressure monitor goes on tomorrow. Shower in the morning. Wear a T-shirt with a loose sleeve.
